title.narrative: Life-Saving and Recovery Assistance for Vulnerable and Disaster Affected Communities in Diinsoor District

description.narrative: ltpgtThe overall objective of the project is to provide timely lifesaving assistance to the most vulnerable disaster(s)-induced displacement affected populations and/or those at risk of being displaced in Dinsoor district of Bay region. The project objective will be achieved through two main interventions: First, provision of Unconditional Cash Transfer (UCT) assistance for a duration of three months the proposed duration of cash assistance has been decided based on global humanitarian best practices, which suggest that sustained multi-month support is often required to stabilize vulnerable households and prevent harmful coping mechanisms such as selling off productive assets, reducing food intake, withdrawal of children from school and increased child labour. This autonomy is critical in dynamic crisis settings where needs can vary drastically from one household to another. Due to resource limitations and in line with the cluster recommendation, NRC will provide 70% of the recommended Minimum Expenditure Basket (MEB) value per HH. The UCT is particularly important in emergency contexts because it offers flexibility and dignity to recipients, allowing them to prioritise their own most urgent needs, like food, water, healthcare, rent, or clothing. Furthermore, UCTs also play a protective role by enabling households to preserve their productive assets (e.g, livestock, farming tools, small businesses), which are often sold off in desperation during crises. Protecting these assets is critical for future recovery and for maintaining a degree of resilience in the face of ongoing uncertainty. The cash transfer values are determined based on national and regional MEB and local market assessments, and a 70% of the recommended transfer value (USD 70) amounting to USD 55 will be released to the selected project participants over a period of three months. This ensures that the cash is adequate to meet a substantial portion of household needs and that it does not inadvertently drive inflation in local markets. Beneficiary households will be selected through a transparent community-based vulnerability targeting approach, conducted in coordination with local authorities and village community elders/committees (VRCs), and guided by the humanitarian principles of impartiality, equity, and transparency.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe second intervention focuses on rehabilitation and/or establishing the small community infrastructures and assets through Cash for Work (CfW) initiatives. The CfW intervention seeks to stimulate early recovery and long-term resilience by engaging communities in meaningful, wage-earning activities tied to local infrastructure rehabilitation, such as water harvesting structures, small-scale irrigation canals and farm-to-market feeder roads. These infrastructures will be carefully selected based on community priorities, local government development plans, and technical feasibility. The goal is not only to inject cash into vulnerable households through paid labor but also to leave behind assets that enhance the community’s ability to cope with future shocks, improve livelihoods, and boost food security. lt/pgtltpgtThe project will engage both skilled and unskilled laborers from the target affected communities. CfW participants will be paid based on daily rates set in line with national labor standards and humanitarian cash programming guidelines, ensuring that wages are fair, sufficient, and do not distort local labor markets. The inclusion of both skilled and unskilled laborers will promote social inclusion and maximize community participation. ltbrgtNRC will make efforts to ensure the inclusion of women, youth, and persons with disabilities by assigning tasks suited to their abilities and ensuring that working conditions are safe, equitable, and non-exploitative. As a standard principle, 'NRC will ensure inclusion of the principles of Do No Harm and gender sensitivity.ltbrgtlt/pgt
